name: Chilean Landscapes: Eye-level vs Aerial Images
description:
Faithful replication of the questionnaire (Appendix C) in Altamirano, A., Gonzalez-Suhr, C., Marien, C., Catalán, G., Miranda, A., Prado, M., Tits, L., Vieli, L., & Meli, P. (2020). Landscape disturbance gradients: The importance of the type of scene when evaluating landscape preferences and perceptions. Land 9(9):306. https://doi.org/10.3390/land9090306

Participants answer the paper's "Personal data 1" (four wellbeing questions, 1–10) and "Personal data 2" (gender, age, occupation, the commune of La Araucanía they live in, urban/rural/semi-rural, origin, time in the area, education). They then see the paper's 12 eye-level photographs (Appendix A) and afterwards its 12 aerial images (Appendix B), one at a time and in random order within each block: three of each of four landscapes along a disturbance gradient (Freire, Lumaco, Pucón, Curarrehue). For each image they rate "I like this place for living / for visiting", "This place makes me feel at risk", "This place is nice", "This place makes me feel good" (1 = totally disagree … 7 = totally agree) and two seven-point bipolar scales: natural … altered, and how the place affects the people who live in it, positively … negatively.

Original study: 107 people (online and in a university computer lab, October 2015 – February 2016). Preferences and perceptions were higher with eye-level (4.0) than aerial images (3.7); preferences generally fell as landscape disturbance rose, consistently with aerial images but masked with eye-level photographs.

Analysis as in the paper: means per landscape and image type for preference to live, preference to visit, scenic beauty (nice), well-being (feel good), risk and disturbance degree (natural … altered); randomized-block ANOVA with landscape, image type and their interaction, with Tukey post hoc tests.

Differences from the original study: (1) the paper's main text lists "This place is natural" as the sixth sentence; we follow Appendix C, which asks it as a natural … altered bipolar scale (coded 1 = too natural … 7 = too altered) and also contains the "affects the people who live in it" scale, which the paper does not analyse; (2) a short introduction and a one-line note before the aerial block are ours; (3) English only; the commune list is that of the paper's questionnaire, so people outside La Araucanía answer "Other".

Images: Appendices A and B of the open-access article (CC BY 4.0); the aerial images are Google Earth views (1:10,000) as used and credited in the paper. Shown with credit for research; the template is removed if the authors object.
